title: Quiz leaderboard ranking
scenario: Two students with the same score get ranks 3 and 4, and the 'top 10' sometimes shows 11 names.
stack: Spring Boot 4.1.1 · Java 25 · Comparator chains · PriorityQueue top-N · competition and dense ranking · MockMvc
simulation: Quizzes, students and scores are demo data, not Shikshalab's. The X-Student-Id header stands in for a signed-in student; a real app takes the student from the login, never from a header.

Level 1, about 5 minutes. Plain language: no code.

The problem in real life

  1. Two students, one score

    Kabir and Meera both score 88. The board shows Kabir 3rd and Meera 4th, only because of the order rows came back in. Meera's parents write in.

  2. A quick fix, a new bug

    Equal scores now share a rank, and "top 10" becomes "rank 10 or better". When two students tie for 10th, the top 10 shows 11 names.

  3. The fix

    Rank by score so ties share a rank; show at most N rows, ordered by score, then time, then id; say how many tied students did not fit.

A rank comes from the score, not from where a row happens to sit in a list.

What are we building?

GET /quizzes/{id}/leaderboard?top=10 shows the best students with their ranks, and …/leaderboard/me shows a student their own rank among everyone.

An everyday analogy

A school sports day. Two children tie for silver: both get silver, and the next child is 4th. The notice board has room for ten names; if there are two 10th places, the board says "and 1 more tied" instead of squeezing in an eleventh.

How it works in 4 steps

  1. Order attempts: higher score first, then less time, then student id.
  2. Keep the best N with a small heap, without sorting all 2,000.
  3. Give ranks: equal scores share the rank of the first of them.
  4. Count how many students tied with the last row did not fit.
Check yourself: Saanvi and Reyansh both scored 70. Saanvi took 240 seconds, Reyansh 270. What are their ranks?

Both 10th: ranks come from the score. Saanvi is shown first because she was faster, and in a top 10 she is the one that fits.

What this station is not

  • No live updates. The board is computed per request.
  • No login. A header stands in for the signed-in student.
  • One attempt per student. Challenge 2 allows retries.

Key terms

TermSimple meaningEveryday exampleIn this project
Competition rankingEqual scores share a rank, and the next rank skips: 1, 2, 2, 4.Two runners tie for silver; nobody gets bronze; the next is 4th.rank
Dense rankingEqual scores share a rank, and the next rank does not skip: 1, 2, 2, 3.Counting distinct scores above you.denseRank
Tie-breakA rule that orders equal items, here only for display.Who finished first, among equal marks.time taken, then student id
ComparatorA rule that says which of two items comes first.The judging criteria, in order.Leaderboard.ORDER

Priority queue (heap)A collection that always knows its smallest item.A queue where the weakest card is always on top, ready to drop.PriorityQueue

Level 2. What a teammate hands you before you build.

Business problem

Shikshalab (a fictional learning app) shows quiz leaderboards. Two students with the same score get ranks 3 and 4, and the "top 10" sometimes shows 11 names.

Acceptance criteria

On quiz 3, "Algebra sprint": 12 students, ties at 3rd, 6th and 10th.

  1. Given Kabir and Meera both at 88, then both are rank 3 (dense 3), Kabir shown first (250 s against 310 s), and the next student is rank 5 (dense 4).
  2. Given top=10 with a tie for 10th, then exactly 10 rows, the faster of the two shown, and moreTiedAtCutoff: 1.
  3. Given Reyansh asks for his place, then rank 10, dense 8, of 12, though he is not in the top 10 rows.
  4. Given equal score and equal time, then the same rank, ordered by student id, the same on every request.
  5. Given an unknown quiz, or a student who did not attempt it, 404; top outside 1 to 100, or a missing or malformed student id, 400.

Requirements

  • Ranks depend on the score only; time and id decide only the display order.
  • Top N is at most N rows; ties beyond the cut are counted.
  • Top N uses a heap of N + 1, not a sort of every attempt.
  • Student ids normalised with Locale.ROOT.

Learning objectives

  • Tell competition from dense ranking, and compute both.
  • Build a comparator chain, and know what reversed() applies to.
  • Find the top N with a PriorityQueue.
  • Define "top N" precisely when there are ties.

The trap

Plausible but wrong

Ranking by list position, so tied scores get different ranks.

The first test ranks by position: Kabir and Meera, both 88, get 3 and 4. The second shows the quick fix: shared ranks, but "rank 10 or better" gives 11 names. The third shows the fix: ten rows, shared ranks, and one more tied counted. While building, each fix was undone once. Ranking by position turned 4 tests red, and a heap that keeps the worst 9. No time tie-break turned 1 red, no cutoff count 4, counting equal scores as ahead in "me" 2, and dense equal to competition ranks 2.

package com.shikshalab.leaderboard;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

/** The first test written for this station: both complaints, reproduced on quiz 3, and the fix. */
class ListPositionRankTrapTest {

    @Test
    void rankingByPositionGivesEqualScoresDifferentRanks() {
        var old = OldLeaderboard.byPosition(Quizzes.ALGEBRA_SPRINT.attempts());
        assertThat(old.get(2).score()).isEqualTo(old.get(3).score()).isEqualTo(88);   // Kabir and Meera, both 88
        assertThat(old.get(2).rank()).isEqualTo(3);
        assertThat(old.get(3).rank()).isEqualTo(4);
    }

    @Test
    void theQuickFixShowsElevenNamesInTheTopTen() {
        assertThat(OldLeaderboard.quickFixTop(Quizzes.ALGEBRA_SPRINT.attempts(), 10)).hasSize(11);   // two students tied at 10th
    }

    @Test
    void theFixSharesRanksAndShowsAtMostTenCountingTheRest() {
        var board = new Leaderboard(new Quizzes()).top(3, 10);
        assertThat(board.rows()).hasSize(10);
        assertThat(board.rows().get(2).rank()).isEqualTo(board.rows().get(3).rank()).isEqualTo(3);
        assertThat(board.rows().getLast().name()).isEqualTo("Saanvi");   // 70 in 240 s, faster than Reyansh's 70 in 270 s
        assertThat(board.moreTiedAtCutoff()).isEqualTo(1);
    }
}
package com.shikshalab.leaderboard;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Comparator;
import java.util.List;

/** The leaderboard before the fix, kept only in tests: first by list position, then the quick fix. */
final class OldLeaderboard {

    record OldRow(int rank, String name, int score) {
    }

    private OldLeaderboard() {
    }

    /** Version 1: the rank is the position in the sorted list. */
    static List<OldRow> byPosition(List<Attempt> attempts) {
        List<Attempt> sorted = new ArrayList<>(attempts);
        sorted.sort(Comparator.comparingInt(Attempt::score).reversed());
        List<OldRow> rows = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < sorted.size(); i++) {
            rows.add(new OldRow(i + 1, sorted.get(i).name(), sorted.get(i).score()));
        }
        return rows;
    }

    /** Version 2, the quick fix: equal scores share a rank, and "top 10" became "rank 10 or better". */
    static List<OldRow> quickFixTop(List<Attempt> attempts, int top) {
        List<OldRow> positions = byPosition(attempts);
        List<OldRow> rows = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < positions.size(); i++) {
            OldRow r = positions.get(i);
            int rank = i > 0 && positions.get(i - 1).score() == r.score() ? rows.get(i - 1).rank() : i + 1;
            rows.add(new OldRow(rank, r.name(), r.score()));
        }
        return rows.stream().filter(r -> r.rank() <= top).toList();
    }
}

package com.shikshalab.leaderboard;

import jakarta.validation.constraints.Max;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Min;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Pattern;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestHeader;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

import java.util.Locale;

@RestController
class LeaderboardController {

    private final Leaderboard leaderboard;

    LeaderboardController(Leaderboard leaderboard) {
        this.leaderboard = leaderboard;
    }

    @GetMapping("/quizzes/{id}/leaderboard")
    Leaderboard.Board top(@PathVariable long id, @RequestParam(defaultValue = "10") @Min(1) @Max(100) int top) {
        return leaderboard.top(id, top);
    }

    /**
     * The caller's own place. X-Student-Id stands in for the signed-in student (demo): a real app takes it from the
     * login token, never from a header the client chooses.
     */
    @GetMapping("/quizzes/{id}/leaderboard/me")
    Leaderboard.MyPlace me(@PathVariable long id,
                           @RequestHeader("X-Student-Id") @Pattern(regexp = "(?i)S-\\d{4}", message = "must look like S-1003") String studentId) {
        return leaderboard.me(id, studentId.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT));
    }
}

src/main/java/com/shikshalab/leaderboard/Leaderboard.java

Does
The order, the top N, the ranks, and your place.
Why
One comparator for the display order; ranks from the score alone; a heap of N + 1.
Without it
Rank = position + 1, and top N = "rank N or better".
  • comparingInt(score).reversed() reverses only the score; the time and id keys keep their natural order.
  • The heap uses ORDER.reversed() so its head is the worst of the best, ready to drop.
  • A row's rank: the previous row's rank on equal scores, its position otherwise. Correct because every higher score is already in the list.
package com.shikshalab.leaderboard;

import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Comparator;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.PriorityQueue;

/**
 * Ranks are by score only, so equal scores share a rank: competition ranking ("1, 2, 2, 4"), with the dense rank
 * ("1, 2, 2, 3") alongside. Inside a tie, rows are shown faster first, then by student id, so the order is the same
 * on every request. "Top N" is at most N rows; anyone tied with the last row who did not fit is counted, not shown.
 */
@Service
class Leaderboard {

    /** Higher score first; on equal scores, less time first; then student id, so no two rows compare equal. */
    static final Comparator<Attempt> ORDER = Comparator.comparingInt(Attempt::score).reversed()
            .thenComparingInt(Attempt::seconds)
            .thenComparing(Attempt::studentId);

    record Row(int rank, int denseRank, String studentId, String name, int score, int seconds) {
    }

    record Board(long quizId, String title, int participants, List<Row> rows, int moreTiedAtCutoff) {
    }

    record MyPlace(long quizId, String studentId, String name, int score, int seconds, int rank, int denseRank, int participants) {
    }

    private final Quizzes quizzes;

    Leaderboard(Quizzes quizzes) {
        this.quizzes = quizzes;
    }

    Board top(long quizId, int n) {
        Quiz quiz = quiz(quizId);
        List<Attempt> best = topN(quiz.attempts(), n);
        List<Row> rows = new ArrayList<>(best.size());
        for (int i = 0; i < best.size(); i++) {
            Attempt a = best.get(i);
            Row previous = i == 0 ? null : rows.get(i - 1);
            boolean tied = previous != null && previous.score() == a.score();
            // Every higher score is already in the list (it is sorted by score first), so position works for the first of a tie.
            int rank = tied ? previous.rank() : i + 1;
            int dense = tied ? previous.denseRank() : (previous == null ? 1 : previous.denseRank() + 1);
            rows.add(new Row(rank, dense, a.studentId(), a.name(), a.score(), a.seconds()));
        }
        int more = 0;
        if (!best.isEmpty()) {
            int lastScore = best.getLast().score();
            more = (int) (quiz.attempts().stream().filter(a -> a.score() == lastScore).count() - best.stream().filter(a -> a.score() == lastScore).count());
        }
        return new Board(quiz.id(), quiz.title(), quiz.attempts().size(), rows, more);
    }

    /** The best n, sorted. A heap of at most n + 1 attempts: O(attempts × log n), and memory for n, not for everyone. */
    static List<Attempt> topN(List<Attempt> attempts, int n) {
        PriorityQueue<Attempt> heap = new PriorityQueue<>(ORDER.reversed());   // the worst of the best on top, to drop
        for (Attempt a : attempts) {
            heap.offer(a);
            if (heap.size() > n) {
                heap.poll();
            }
        }
        List<Attempt> best = new ArrayList<>(heap);
        best.sort(ORDER);
        return best;
    }

    MyPlace me(long quizId, String studentId) {
        Quiz quiz = quiz(quizId);
        Attempt mine = quiz.attempts().stream().filter(a -> a.studentId().equals(studentId)).findFirst()
                .orElseThrow(() -> problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No attempt", studentId + " has not attempted quiz " + quizId + "."));
        int rank = 1 + (int) quiz.attempts().stream().filter(a -> a.score() > mine.score()).count();
        int dense = 1 + (int) quiz.attempts().stream().mapToInt(Attempt::score).filter(s -> s > mine.score()).distinct().count();
        return new MyPlace(quizId, studentId, mine.name(), mine.score(), mine.seconds(), rank, dense, quiz.attempts().size());
    }

    private Quiz quiz(long quizId) {
        return quizzes.find(quizId).orElseThrow(() -> problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Quiz not found", "No quiz " + quizId + "."));
    }

    private static ErrorResponseException problem(HttpStatus status, String title, String detail) {
        ProblemDetail p = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(status, detail);
        p.setTitle(title);
        return new ErrorResponseException(status, p, null);
    }
}

package com.shikshalab.leaderboard;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.Random;

/**
 * Demo quizzes. Quiz 3 is small enough to check by hand: ties at rank 3, at rank 6 and at rank 10. Quiz 7 has 2,000
 * generated attempts (fixed seed), for the top-N code to work on something larger.
 */

package com.shikshalab.leaderboard;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.ValueSource;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Comparator;
import java.util.List;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.groups.Tuple.tuple;

/** Ranking rules without Spring. */
class RankingTest {

    static final Quizzes QUIZZES = new Quizzes();
    static final Leaderboard BOARD = new Leaderboard(QUIZZES);

    @Test
    void competitionAndDenseRanksOnTheHandCheckedQuiz() {
        assertThat(BOARD.top(3, 12).rows()).extracting(Leaderboard.Row::name, Leaderboard.Row::rank, Leaderboard.Row::denseRank)
                .containsExactly(tuple("Aarav", 1, 1), tuple("Diya", 2, 2), tuple("Kabir", 3, 3), tuple("Meera", 3, 3),
                        tuple("Rohan", 5, 4), tuple("Vihaan", 6, 5), tuple("Ananya", 6, 5), tuple("Ishita", 8, 6),
                        tuple("Arjun", 9, 7), tuple("Saanvi", 10, 8), tuple("Reyansh", 10, 8), tuple("Tara", 12, 9));
    }

    @Test
    void equalScoreAndEqualTimeAreOrderedByStudentIdAndShareTheRank() {
        List<Attempt> twins = List.of(new Attempt("S-0002", "B", 50, 100), new Attempt("S-0001", "A", 50, 100), new Attempt("S-0003", "C", 90, 500));
        List<Attempt> best = Leaderboard.topN(twins, 3);
        assertThat(best).extracting(Attempt::studentId).containsExactly("S-0003", "S-0001", "S-0002");
    }

    @Test
    void reversingTheWholeChainWouldPutTheSlowerFirst() {
        // A common slip: reversed() at the end reverses every key, so on equal scores the slower student wins.
        Comparator<Attempt> wrong = Comparator.comparingInt(Attempt::score).thenComparingInt(Attempt::seconds).reversed();
        Attempt fast = new Attempt("S-0001", "fast", 70, 240);
        Attempt slow = new Attempt("S-0002", "slow", 70, 270);
        assertThat(wrong.compare(fast, slow)).isPositive();              // fast sorts after slow
        assertThat(Leaderboard.ORDER.compare(fast, slow)).isNegative();  // the real order: fast first
    }

    @ParameterizedTest
    @ValueSource(ints = {1, 10, 100, 1_999, 2_000, 2_500})
    void theHeapGivesTheSameTopNAsSortingEveryone(int n) {
        List<Attempt> all = new ArrayList<>(QUIZZES.find(7).orElseThrow().attempts());
        all.sort(Leaderboard.ORDER);
        assertThat(Leaderboard.topN(QUIZZES.find(7).orElseThrow().attempts(), n)).isEqualTo(all.subList(0, Math.min(n, all.size())));
    }

    @Test
    void myPlaceMatchesTheBoardForEveryStudent() {
        for (Leaderboard.Row row : BOARD.top(7, 100).rows()) {
            var me = BOARD.me(7, row.studentId());
            assertThat(me.rank()).as(row.studentId()).isEqualTo(row.rank());
            assertThat(me.denseRank()).as(row.studentId()).isEqualTo(row.denseRank());
        }
    }

    @Test
    void theCutoffCountIsEveryoneTiedWithTheLastRowWhoDidNotFit() {
        var board = BOARD.top(7, 100);
        int lastScore = board.rows().getLast().score();
        long tiedOverall = QUIZZES.find(7).orElseThrow().attempts().stream().filter(a -> a.score() == lastScore).count();
        long tiedShown = board.rows().stream().filter(r -> r.score() == lastScore).count();
        assertThat(board.moreTiedAtCutoff()).isEqualTo(tiedOverall - tiedShown).isPositive();
    }
}

package com.shikshalab.leaderboard;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Comparator;
import java.util.List;

/** The leaderboard before the fix, kept only in tests: first by list position, then the quick fix. */
final class OldLeaderboard {

    record OldRow(int rank, String name, int score) {
    }

    private OldLeaderboard() {
    }

    /** Version 1: the rank is the position in the sorted list. */
    static List<OldRow> byPosition(List<Attempt> attempts) {
        List<Attempt> sorted = new ArrayList<>(attempts);
        sorted.sort(Comparator.comparingInt(Attempt::score).reversed());
        List<OldRow> rows = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < sorted.size(); i++) {
            rows.add(new OldRow(i + 1, sorted.get(i).name(), sorted.get(i).score()));
        }
        return rows;
    }

    /** Version 2, the quick fix: equal scores share a rank, and "top 10" became "rank 10 or better". */
    static List<OldRow> quickFixTop(List<Attempt> attempts, int top) {
        List<OldRow> positions = byPosition(attempts);
        List<OldRow> rows = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < positions.size(); i++) {
            OldRow r = positions.get(i);
            int rank = i > 0 && positions.get(i - 1).score() == r.score() ? rows.get(i - 1).rank() : i + 1;
            rows.add(new OldRow(rank, r.name(), r.score()));
        }
        return rows.stream().filter(r -> r.rank() <= top).toList();
    }
}

package com.shikshalab.leaderboard;

import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Comparator;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.PriorityQueue;
import java.util.function.BinaryOperator;
import java.util.function.Function;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/**
 * Ranks are by score only, so equal scores share a rank: competition ranking ("1, 2, 2, 4"), with the dense rank
 * ("1, 2, 2, 3") alongside. Inside a tie, rows are shown faster first, then by student id, so the order is the same
 * on every request. "Top N" is at most N rows; anyone tied with the last row who did not fit is counted, not shown.
 */
@Service
class Leaderboard {

    /** Higher score first; on equal scores, less time first; then student id, so no two rows compare equal. */
    static final Comparator<Attempt> ORDER = Comparator.comparingInt(Attempt::score).reversed()
            .thenComparingInt(Attempt::seconds)
            .thenComparing(Attempt::studentId);

    record Row(int rank, int denseRank, String studentId, String name, int score, int seconds) {
    }

    record Board(long quizId, String title, int participants, List<Row> rows, int moreTiedAtCutoff) {
    }

    record MyPlace(long quizId, String studentId, String name, int score, int seconds, int rank, int denseRank, int participants) {
    }

    private final Quizzes quizzes;

    Leaderboard(Quizzes quizzes) {
        this.quizzes = quizzes;
    }

    Board top(long quizId, int n) {
        Quiz quiz = quiz(quizId);
        List<Attempt> everyone = bestPerStudent(quiz.attempts());
        List<Attempt> best = topN(everyone, n);
        List<Row> rows = ranked(best);
        int more = 0;
        if (!best.isEmpty()) {
            int lastScore = best.getLast().score();
            more = (int) (everyone.stream().filter(a -> a.score() == lastScore).count() - best.stream().filter(a -> a.score() == lastScore).count());
        }
        return new Board(quiz.id(), quiz.title(), everyone.size(), rows, more);
    }

    /** Ranks for a list sorted by ORDER that starts at the top of the board. */
    static List<Row> ranked(List<Attempt> sorted) {
        List<Row> rows = new ArrayList<>(sorted.size());
        for (int i = 0; i < sorted.size(); i++) {
            Attempt a = sorted.get(i);
            Row previous = i == 0 ? null : rows.get(i - 1);
            boolean tied = previous != null && previous.score() == a.score();
            int rank = tied ? previous.rank() : i + 1;
            int dense = tied ? previous.denseRank() : (previous == null ? 1 : previous.denseRank() + 1);
            rows.add(new Row(rank, dense, a.studentId(), a.name(), a.score(), a.seconds()));
        }
        return rows;
    }

    /** Up to k rows either side of the student, ranked over the whole board. */
    List<Row> around(long quizId, String studentId, int k) {
        List<Attempt> everyone = new ArrayList<>(bestPerStudent(quiz(quizId).attempts()));
        everyone.sort(ORDER);
        List<Row> all = ranked(everyone);
        int i = 0;
        while (i < all.size() && !all.get(i).studentId().equals(studentId)) {
            i++;
        }
        if (i == all.size()) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No attempt", studentId + " has not attempted quiz " + quizId + ".");
        }
        return all.subList(Math.max(0, i - k), Math.min(all.size(), i + k + 1));
    }

    /** Each student's best attempt: highest score, then fastest. */
    static List<Attempt> bestPerStudent(List<Attempt> attempts) {
        return List.copyOf(attempts.stream()
                .collect(Collectors.toMap(Attempt::studentId, Function.identity(), BinaryOperator.minBy(ORDER)))
                .values());
    }

    /** The best n, sorted. A heap of at most n + 1 attempts: O(attempts × log n), and memory for n, not for everyone. */
    static List<Attempt> topN(List<Attempt> attempts, int n) {
        PriorityQueue<Attempt> heap = new PriorityQueue<>(ORDER.reversed());   // the worst of the best on top, to drop
        for (Attempt a : attempts) {
            heap.offer(a);
            if (heap.size() > n) {
                heap.poll();
            }
        }
        List<Attempt> best = new ArrayList<>(heap);
        best.sort(ORDER);
        return best;
    }

    MyPlace me(long quizId, String studentId) {
        Quiz quiz = quiz(quizId);
        List<Attempt> everyone = bestPerStudent(quiz.attempts());
        Attempt mine = everyone.stream().filter(a -> a.studentId().equals(studentId)).findFirst()
                .orElseThrow(() -> problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No attempt", studentId + " has not attempted quiz " + quizId + "."));
        int rank = 1 + (int) everyone.stream().filter(a -> a.score() > mine.score()).count();
        int dense = 1 + (int) everyone.stream().mapToInt(Attempt::score).filter(s -> s > mine.score()).distinct().count();
        return new MyPlace(quizId, studentId, mine.name(), mine.score(), mine.seconds(), rank, dense, everyone.size());
    }

    private Quiz quiz(long quizId) {
        return quizzes.find(quizId).orElseThrow(() -> problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Quiz not found", "No quiz " + quizId + "."));
    }

    private static ErrorResponseException problem(HttpStatus status, String title, String detail) {
        ProblemDetail p = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(status, detail);
        p.setTitle(title);
        return new ErrorResponseException(status, p, null);
    }
}

    }

    private final Quizzes quizzes;

    Leaderboard(Quizzes quizzes) {
        this.quizzes = quizzes;
    }

    Board top(long quizId, int n) {
        Quiz quiz = quiz(quizId);
        List<Attempt> everyone = bestPerStudent(quiz.attempts());
        List<Attempt> best = topN(everyone, n);
        List<Row> rows = ranked(best);
        int more = 0;
        if (!best.isEmpty()) {
            int lastScore = best.getLast().score();
            more = (int) (everyone.stream().filter(a -> a.score() == lastScore).count() - best.stream().filter(a -> a.score() == lastScore).count());
        }
        return new Board(quiz.id(), quiz.title(), everyone.size(), rows, more);
    }

    /** Ranks for a list sorted by ORDER that starts at the top of the board. */
    static List<Row> ranked(List<Attempt> sorted) {
        List<Row> rows = new ArrayList<>(sorted.size());
        for (int i = 0; i < sorted.size(); i++) {
            Attempt a = sorted.get(i);
            Row previous = i == 0 ? null : rows.get(i - 1);
            boolean tied = previous != null && previous.score() == a.score();
            int rank = tied ? previous.rank() : i + 1;
            int dense = tied ? previous.denseRank() : (previous == null ? 1 : previous.denseRank() + 1);
            rows.add(new Row(rank, dense, a.studentId(), a.name(), a.score(), a.seconds()));
        }
        return rows;
    }

    /** Up to k rows either side of the student, ranked over the whole board. */
    List<Row> around(long quizId, String studentId, int k) {
        List<Attempt> everyone = new ArrayList<>(bestPerStudent(quiz(quizId).attempts()));
        everyone.sort(ORDER);
        List<Row> all = ranked(everyone);
        int i = 0;
        while (i < all.size() && !all.get(i).studentId().equals(studentId)) {
            i++;
        }
        if (i == all.size()) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No attempt", studentId + " has not attempted quiz " + quizId + ".");
        }
        return all.subList(Math.max(0, i - k), Math.min(all.size(), i + k + 1));
    }

    /** Each student's best attempt: highest score, then fastest. */
    static List<Attempt> bestPerStudent(List<Attempt> attempts) {
        return List.copyOf(attempts.stream()
                .collect(Collectors.toMap(Attempt::studentId, Function.identity(), BinaryOperator.minBy(ORDER)))
                .values());
    }

    /** The best n, sorted. A heap of at most n + 1 attempts: O(attempts × log n), and memory for n, not for everyone. */
    static List<Attempt> topN(List<Attempt> attempts, int n) {
        PriorityQueue<Attempt> heap = new PriorityQueue<>(ORDER.reversed());   // the worst of the best on top, to drop
        for (Attempt a : attempts) {
            heap.offer(a);
            if (heap.size() > n) {
                heap.poll();
            }
        }
        List<Attempt> best = new ArrayList<>(heap);
        best.sort(ORDER);
        return best;
    }

    MyPlace me(long quizId, String studentId) {
        Quiz quiz = quiz(quizId);
        List<Attempt> everyone = bestPerStudent(quiz.attempts());
        Attempt mine = everyone.stream().filter(a -> a.studentId().equals(studentId)).findFirst()
                .orElseThrow(() -> problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No attempt", studentId + " has not attempted quiz " + quizId + "."));
        int rank = 1 + (int) everyone.stream().filter(a -> a.score() > mine.score()).count();
        int dense = 1 + (int) everyone.stream().mapToInt(Attempt::score).filter(s -> s > mine.score()).distinct().count();
        return new MyPlace(quizId, studentId, mine.name(), mine.score(), mine.seconds(), rank, dense, everyone.size());
    }

    private Quiz quiz(long quizId) {
        return quizzes.find(quizId).orElseThrow(() -> problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Quiz not found", "No quiz " + quizId + "."));
    }

    private static ErrorResponseException problem(HttpStatus status, String title, String detail) {
        ProblemDetail p = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(status, detail);
        p.setTitle(title);
        return new ErrorResponseException(status, p, null);
    }
}

Challenge 3 · design on paper, no code

A live board for two lakh students

A national quiz has 2,00,000 students submitting in the same 10 minutes, and the board must update every few seconds. Compare recomputing from all attempts, keeping a sorted structure in memory, and a sorted set in a cache such as Valkey. How does each one answer "my rank" for a student at 1,50,000th place?

Implementation approach

  1. Write the trap test on a quiz small enough to rank by hand.
  2. Decide the rules in words: what decides a rank, what decides display order, what "top N" means with ties.
  3. Write the comparator, then the heap, then the ranks.
  4. Check the heap against a full sort, and "me" against the board, on 2,000 attempts.

Design alternatives and trade-offs

Database design

None in this station. In SQL, rank() over (order by score desc) and dense_rank() over (…) compute both rankings, with order by score desc, seconds, student_id limit 10 for the display order; unique (quiz_id, student_id) on attempts enforces one attempt each.

A Foundations station: the considerations to know, no runbook.

Fairness
Whatever decides ties must be written in the quiz rules before students start. Changing it afterwards changes who "won".
Identity
"Me" must come from the login. A header the client sets would let anyone see anyone's place.
Scale
Recomputing per request is fine for thousands of attempts; for lakhs with frequent reads, keep a sorted structure or cache the board for a few seconds.
Children's data
Leaderboards for minors often show first names only, or let a student hide their name; check the school's and the law's rules on children's data.

Interview takeaways

Competition vs dense ranking?

Both give equal values the same rank. Competition skips the following ranks (1, 2, 2, 4); dense does not (1, 2, 2, 3). SQL has rank() and dense_rank().

How do you find the top N of a large list efficiently?

A min-heap of size N: offer each item, poll when it exceeds N. O(n log N) time and O(N) memory, versus O(n log n) for a full sort.

What does Comparator.reversed() reverse?

The whole comparator it is called on. comparingInt(score).reversed().thenComparing(time) reverses only the score; ...thenComparing(time).reversed() reverses both.

Why end a comparator with a unique key?

Otherwise equal items keep whatever order the input had, which can change between requests, so the board flickers.

How do you compute one student's rank without sorting?

Count the students with a higher score and add one (competition); count distinct higher scores and add one (dense).
